questions.explanation: A liquid keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container.

questions.explanation: The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin (K).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Gases can be compressed easily because
options: their particles have very large spaces between them
questions.explanation: Large inter-particle spaces in a gas allow the particles to be pushed closer together.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Wet clothes dry faster on a windy day than on a still day because the wind
options: makes the water in the clothes boil
carries away water vapour, which speeds up evaporation
freezes the water on the clothes
increases the humidity of the air near the clothes
questions.explanation: Moving air removes water vapour near the cloth, so more water evaporates in the same time.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: While ice is melting in a beaker over a flame, the thermometer keeps reading 0 °C even though heat is supplied. This is because
options: all the heat is lost to the surroundings
the heat supplied is used to overcome the forces between particles (latent heat of fusion)
ice does not absorb heat while melting
questions.explanation: The heat of fusion breaks the particle arrangement of the solid, so the temperature does not rise until all the ice has melted.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is evaporation? Name two factors that increase its rate.
questions.answer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour at any temperature below its boiling point, taking place at the surface. Its rate increases with a larger surface area and with a higher temperature (also with less humidity and more wind).
keyPoints: Liquid changes to vapour below boiling point
Rate rises with temperature, wind or lower humidity
questions.explanation: Faster-moving surface particles escape into the air, so conditions that help them escape raise the rate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do we feel cooler after sweating when we sit under a fan?
questions.answer: Sweat on the skin evaporates. The particles of water need energy to change into vapour and take this latent heat from the body, which cools us. The fan blows away the vapour and makes evaporation faster.
keyPoints: Evaporation takes heat from the body
questions.explanation: Evaporation is a cooling process because the escaping particles absorb heat from the surface.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a pure substance?
questions.explanation: Distilled water contains only water, a compound, so it is a pure substance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a mixture?
questions.explanation: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc, so it is a homogeneous mixture.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Common salt is obtained from sea water by
questions.explanation: On heating sea water the water evaporates and the salt is left behind.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which method separates a mixture of common salt and ammonium chloride?
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride sublimes on heating while common salt does not.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following shows the Tyndall effect?
questions.explanation: Milk is a colloid whose particles are large enough to scatter a beam of light.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A separating funnel can be used to separate oil from water because the two liquids
options: are immiscible and form separate layers
questions.explanation: Immiscible liquids form two layers, and the lower one can be run off through the tap.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A beam of light is clearly visible when passed through a liquid. The particles do not settle on standing and cannot be removed by ordinary filtration. The liquid is a
questions.explanation: A colloid scatters light but its particles stay dispersed and pass through filter paper; a suspension would settle.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Give two differences between a compound and a mixture.
questions.answer: A compound is formed by chemical combination of elements in a fixed ratio by mass and has properties different from its elements. A mixture can have any proportion of its components, which keep their own properties and can be separated by physical methods.
keyPoints: Compound has fixed composition, mixture variable
questions.explanation: Compounds involve chemical bonding; mixtures are only physically combined.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How would you separate a mixture of sand, common salt and iron filings?
questions.answer: First pass a magnet over the mixture to remove the iron filings. Add water to the remaining mixture to dissolve the salt and filter it, so the sand stays on the filter paper. Evaporate the filtrate to get the salt.
questions.explanation: Each step uses a different property: magnetism, solubility and volatility of the solvent.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The law of conservation of mass was put forward by
questions.explanation: Lavoisier showed that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical symbol of sodium is
questions.explanation: The symbol Na comes from the Latin name natrium.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.explanation: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many atoms are present in one molecule of sulphuric acid, H2SO4?
questions.explanation: 2 hydrogen + 1 sulphur + 4 oxygen = 7 atoms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The molecular mass of carbon dioxide, CO2, is (C = 12 u, O = 16 u)

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many moles are present in 11 g of carbon dioxide (molar mass 44 g/mol)?
questions.explanation: Moles = mass / molar mass = 11 / 44 = 0.25.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Samples of pure water from a river and from rain are both found to contain hydrogen and oxygen in the mass ratio 1 : 8. Which law does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: A pure compound always has its elements in a fixed ratio by mass, whatever its source.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the law of conservation of mass and give an example.
questions.answer: In a chemical reaction the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products; mass is neither created nor destroyed. For example, when 12 g of carbon burns in 32 g of oxygen, 44 g of carbon dioxide is formed.
keyPoints: Mass is neither created nor destroyed
Total mass of reactants equals products
questions.explanation: Atoms are only rearranged in a reaction, so total mass stays the same.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Calculate the number of molecules in 0.5 mole of a gas. (Avogadro constant = 6.022 × 10^23 per mole)
questions.answer: Number of molecules = moles × Avogadro constant = 0.5 × 6.022 × 10^23 = 3.011 × 10^23 molecules.
questions.explanation: One mole contains 6.022 × 10^23 particles, so half a mole contains half that number.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Who discovered the atomic nucleus through the gold foil experiment?
questions.explanation: Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment led to the nuclear model of the atom.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which subatomic particle carries no electric charge?
questions.explanation: The neutron is electrically neutral.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The electron was discovered by
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron and proposed the plum-pudding model.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of
questions.explanation: Atomic number Z is the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that the M shell (third shell) can hold?
questions.explanation: The 2n² rule gives 2 × 3² = 18 electrons.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An atom has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 1. Its valency is
questions.explanation: The atom has one electron in its outermost shell and can lose it, so its valency is 1.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Two atoms both have mass number 40, but their atomic numbers are 18 and 20. They are called
questions.explanation: Atoms of different elements with the same mass number are isobars.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two drawbacks of Rutherford's model of the atom.
questions.answer: According to the model, electrons revolving around the nucleus would be accelerating and lose energy, so they should spiral into the nucleus and the atom would collapse. The model also could not explain why atoms are stable.
questions.explanation: Bohr's model overcame this with fixed energy levels (shells).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Chlorine occurs as two isotopes, Cl-35 and Cl-37, yet its atomic mass is given as 35.5 u. Explain.
questions.answer: The atomic mass of an element is the average of the masses of its isotopes weighted by their natural abundance. Cl-35 is more abundant (about three times Cl-37), so the average is 35.5 u, not a whole number.
questions.explanation: No single chlorine atom has mass 35.5 u; this is an average over the natural mixture.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Who first observed cells in a thin slice of cork?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke saw the box-like cells of cork under a microscope in 1665.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which cell organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release the energy of food as ATP.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The cell wall of a plant cell is mainly made of
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are made chiefly of cellulose.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Who discovered the nucleus in the cell?
questions.explanation: Robert Brown described the nucleus in 1831.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Osmosis is the movement of
options: water across a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to lower water concentration
solute particles from low to high concentration using energy
gases from a region of high to low pressure
solid particles through the cell wall
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the diffusion of water through a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which organelles are known as the suicide bags of the cell?
questions.explanation: If a cell is damaged, lysosomes burst and their enzymes digest the cell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Red blood cells are placed in a very concentrated salt solution. They shrink because
options: water enters the cells by osmosis
water leaves the cells by osmosis
questions.explanation: The surrounding solution is more concentrated, so water moves out of the cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
questions.answer: A prokaryotic cell has no well-defined nucleus (no nuclear membrane) and no membrane-bound organelles, while a eukaryotic cell has a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller, for example bacteria.
questions.explanation: The key difference is the presence or absence of a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Potato cubes are placed in distilled water and in a concentrated sugar solution. Predict what happens to each and explain.
questions.answer: In distilled water the potato cubes gain water by osmosis and become firm and larger. In concentrated sugar solution they lose water by osmosis and shrink, because water moves toward the region with the lower water concentration.
keyPoints: Distilled water: water enters, cube swells
Sugar solution: water leaves, cube shrinks
Water moves by osmosis across the membrane
questions.explanation: Direction of water movement depends on the relative concentration inside and outside the cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which tissue carries water and minerals upward in a plant?
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and minerals from the roots to the leaves.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which structure connects muscle to bone?
questions.explanation: Tendons are strong fibrous tissues that join muscle to bone.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The structural and functional unit of nervous tissue is the
questions.explanation: A neuron is a nerve cell that carries impulses.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which meristem is responsible for the increase in the girth (thickness) of a stem?
questions.explanation: Lateral meristem (cambium) adds to the thickness of stems and roots.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these muscles works under the control of our will?
options: The muscle of the heart wall
The muscle in the wall of the intestine
The muscle that controls the pupil of the eye
The biceps muscle of the arm
questions.explanation: The biceps is a skeletal muscle, which is voluntary.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A leaf that has lost much water droops, and the guard cells of its stomata change shape. The guard cells mainly control
options: the opening and closing of the stomata
the transport of food to the roots
the thickness of the cell wall
the growth in length of the leaf
questions.explanation: Guard cells open and close the stomatal pore, controlling gas exchange and water loss.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Leaf stalks and tender stems bend in the wind without breaking. Which tissue gives them this flexibility?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma has thickened corners that give flexibility with mechanical support.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two differences between xylem and phloem.
questions.answer: Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to other parts, and most of its cells are dead. Phloem transports food (sugars) prepared in leaves to other parts, and its sieve tubes are living cells.
questions.explanation: Together they form the complex conducting tissues of plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What would happen to a shoot if its apical meristem were removed? Give a reason.
questions.answer: The shoot would stop growing in length, because cell division at the tip, which adds new cells that elongate the stem, would no longer take place.
keyPoints: Apical meristem divides at the tip
Division adds cells that elongate stem
questions.explanation: Apical meristem is responsible for the increase in length of shoots and roots.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the SI unit of velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is displacement per unit time, measured in metres per second.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The slope of a distance-time graph gives
questions.explanation: Slope is change in distance divided by change in time, which is speed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these quantities has both magnitude and direction?
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector; the others are scalars.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A car covers 60 km in 1.5 hours. Its average speed is
questions.explanation: Speed = 60 km / 1.5 h = 40 km/h.

questions.q: An athlete completes exactly one full round of a circular track of radius r. Her displacement is
questions.explanation: She ends at the starting point, so the displacement is zero although the distance is 2πr.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A car moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest in 5 s by uniform braking. Taking the direction of motion as positive, its acceleration is
questions.explanation: a = (0 − 20) / 5 = −4 m/s²; the negative sign shows retardation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between distance and displacement.
questions.answer: Distance is the total length of the path travelled and is a scalar that is never negative. Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position with a direction, and it is a vector that can be zero.
keyPoints: Displacement is shortest change in position, vector
Displacement can be zero or negative
questions.explanation: Displacement depends only on end points, distance depends on the path.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A bus increases its speed from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 10 s. Find its acceleration and the distance it covers in this time.
questions.answer: Acceleration a = (30 − 10) / 10 = 2 m/s². Distance s = (v² − u²) / 2a = (900 − 100) / 4 = 200 m.
questions.explanation: Both answers use the equations of uniformly accelerated motion; average speed 20 m/s × 10 s also gives 200 m.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The law of inertia is which of Newton's laws of motion?
questions.explanation: Newton's first law says a body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by an unbalanced force.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of force is the
questions.explanation: One newton is the force that gives a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s².

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The momentum of a body is defined as
questions.explanation: Momentum p = m × v.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What force is needed to give a 5 kg body an acceleration of 3 m/s²?

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A rocket moves forward by throwing hot gases backward. This is an example of
options: the law of conservation of energy
questions.explanation: The gases are pushed back and an equal and opposite force pushes the rocket forward.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Passengers in a bus are thrown forward when the driver brakes suddenly. The reason is that
options: the bus pushes the passengers forward
the passengers' bodies tend to continue in their state of motion
questions.explanation: Inertia keeps the upper body moving forward while the bus slows down.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A 4 kg gun fires a 0.02 kg bullet at 100 m/s. The recoil speed of the gun is
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum, 4 × v = 0.02 × 100, so v = 0.5 m/s.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State Newton's second law of motion and write its mathematical form.
questions.answer: The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied unbalanced force and takes place in the direction of the force. For constant mass, F = ma.
keyPoints: Rate of change of momentum proportional to force
questions.explanation: The law gives the way to measure force from mass and acceleration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a cricketer pull his hands backward while catching a fast cricket ball?
questions.answer: By moving the hands back, the cricketer increases the time over which the ball's momentum is brought to zero. A longer time means a smaller rate of change of momentum, so the force on the hands is smaller and they are not hurt.
keyPoints: Rate of change of momentum decreases
questions.explanation: F = change in momentum / time, so a larger time reduces the force.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity near the Earth's surface is about
questions.explanation: g is approximately 9.8 m/s² on Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Weight of an object is measured in
questions.explanation: Weight is the force of gravity on a body, so its unit is the newton.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the weight of a 10 kg object on Earth? (g = 9.8 m/s²)

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is about one-sixth of that on Earth. A person of mass 60 kg on the Moon has a mass of
questions.explanation: Mass does not depend on location; only the weight changes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A heavy stone and a light feather are dropped together from the same height in a vacuum. They
options: reach the ground at the same time
questions.explanation: With no air resistance every body falls with the same acceleration g.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes
questions.explanation: Force varies inversely as the square of the distance, so doubling d divides F by 4.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the universal law of gravitation.
questions.answer: Every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them, F = G m1 m2 / r².
keyPoints: Inversely proportional to square of distance
questions.explanation: The force acts along the line joining the centres of the two objects.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is the value of g slightly greater at the poles than at the equator?
questions.answer: The Earth is not a perfect sphere; it is slightly flattened at the poles, so the poles are nearer to the centre of the Earth. Since g is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the centre, g is larger at the poles.
keyPoints: Poles are closer to the centre
g varies inversely with square of radius
questions.explanation: A smaller radius at the poles gives a greater value of g.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of work is the
questions.explanation: Work is measured in joules; one joule is one newton-metre.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The energy possessed by a body due to its motion is called
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion, KE = ½mv².

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the potential energy of a 2 kg object at a height of 5 m? (take g = 10 m/s²)

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The kinetic energy of a 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A girl carries a bag and walks along a level road. The work done by the upward force she applies on the bag is
questions.explanation: The force is vertical while the displacement is horizontal, so no work is done by it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A 60 W bulb is switched on for 5 hours. The electrical energy it uses is
questions.explanation: Energy = 0.06 kW × 5 h = 0.3 kWh.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the law of conservation of energy.
questions.answer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be changed from one form into another. The total energy of an isolated system remains constant.
keyPoints: Energy is not created or destroyed
It changes from one form to another
questions.explanation: In every transformation the total amount of energy stays the same.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe the energy changes in a swinging pendulum bob.
questions.answer: At the extreme positions the bob is momentarily at rest and has maximum potential energy. As it swings down, potential energy changes to kinetic energy, which is maximum at the lowest point. The total energy stays constant if air resistance is ignored.
questions.explanation: In reality a little energy is lost as heat, so the pendulum gradually stops.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sound cannot travel through
questions.explanation: Sound needs a material medium to travel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of frequency is the
questions.explanation: One hertz is one oscillation per second.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The audible range of frequency for normal human ears is about
questions.explanation: Humans generally hear sounds from 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sound waves in air are
questions.explanation: Particles of air vibrate back and forth along the direction in which the wave travels.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: To hear a distinct echo, the reflecting surface must be at least about how far from the source of sound (in air, ordinary temperature)?
questions.explanation: The sound must return after at least 0.1 s; at about 344 m/s the surface must be roughly 17 m away.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: We hear thunder some seconds after seeing the lightning because
options: thunder is produced after the lightning
light travels much faster than sound
the sound is absorbed by clouds
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 3 × 10^8 m/s while sound travels at only about 340 m/s in air.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between loudness and pitch of a sound.
questions.answer: Loudness depends on the amplitude of the vibration; a larger amplitude gives a louder sound. Pitch depends on the frequency; a higher frequency gives a higher pitch (shriller sound).
questions.explanation: Amplitude and frequency are different features of a wave.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person fires a gun and hears its echo from a cliff after 2 s. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, how far is the cliff?
questions.answer: The sound travels to the cliff and back, so total distance = 340 × 2 = 680 m. The cliff is half of this distance away, i.e. 340 m.
keyPoints: Path is to the cliff and back
questions.explanation: The echo covers twice the distance to the reflector.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Paddy is sown in the rainy season (June to July) and is a kharif crop.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a rabi crop?
questions.explanation: Wheat is sown in winter and harvested in spring, so it is a rabi crop.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The rearing of fish is called
questions.explanation: Pisciculture means fish farming.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Apiculture is the rearing of
questions.explanation: Apiculture or bee-keeping is done to get honey and wax.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Manure is
options: a chemical fertiliser made in factories
an organic substance made by the decomposition of animal waste and plant residues
a mineral mined from the ground
questions.explanation: Manure is organic and adds nutrients and humus to the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do farmers grow different crops, such as a legume after a cereal, on the same field in succession?
options: To increase the number of weeds
To help maintain soil fertility and reduce pests and diseases
questions.explanation: Crop rotation avoids exhausting the same nutrients and legumes add nitrogen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are macronutrients? Name any three.
questions.answer: Macronutrients are the nutrients that plants need in large quantities. Examples are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulphur.
keyPoints: Needed by plants in large amounts
Three named examples such as N, P, K
questions.explanation: Plants get these six elements from the soil in large amounts.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is intercropping? Give one example and one advantage.
questions.answer: Intercropping is growing two or more crops simultaneously in the same field in a definite pattern of rows. An example is soyabean with maize. Its advantage is that it reduces the risk of crop failure and makes better use of resources.
keyPoints: Two or more crops in definite row pattern
Example such as soyabean with maize
Better use of resources or less pest spread
questions.explanation: The crops chosen need different nutrients so they do not compete much.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In which state of matter are the forces of attraction between particles the weakest?
questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart, so the attraction between them is weakest.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: At normal atmospheric pressure, water boils at
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100 °C, which is 373 K.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The smell of hot food reaches us from the kitchen even from a distance because of
questions.explanation: Particles of the aroma mix with air particles on their own, which is diffusion.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The heat energy needed to change 1 kg of a liquid into gas at its boiling point, without any rise in temperature, is called
questions.explanation: This hidden heat is the latent heat of vaporisation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Solid carbon dioxide is called dry ice because it
options: changes directly from solid to gas without becoming a liquid
is frozen water with no moisture
is carbon dioxide dissolved in ice
is ice stored in dry air
questions.explanation: It sublimes at normal pressure and leaves no liquid behind.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A syringe full of air can be pressed in easily, but a syringe full of water cannot. This is because
options: water particles are lighter than air particles
the spaces between air particles are large, but those between liquid particles are very small
air has less mass than water
questions.explanation: Air can be compressed into its large spaces; liquids are nearly incompressible.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Steam at 100 °C causes more severe burns than boiling water at 100 °C because steam
options: carries extra latent heat of vaporisation that is released when it condenses on the skin
is at a higher temperature than 100 °C
questions.explanation: Condensing steam gives out latent heat in addition to the heat from cooling.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two differences between boiling and evaporation.
questions.answer: Boiling takes place throughout the liquid at one fixed temperature, the boiling point, and is a bulk phenomenon. Evaporation occurs only at the surface, at any temperature below the boiling point, and is a slow process.
keyPoints: Boiling occurs at a fixed temperature
Boiling is throughout the liquid; evaporation is at the surface
questions.explanation: Both change a liquid into vapour but under different conditions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are cotton clothes preferred in summer?
questions.answer: Cotton absorbs sweat and exposes it to the air over a large surface, so the sweat evaporates quickly. Evaporation takes heat from the body and keeps us cool.
questions.explanation: Synthetic fabrics absorb little sweat, so they cool less.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an element?
questions.explanation: Sulphur consists of only one kind of atom.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a solution of common salt in water, the salt is called the
questions.explanation: The substance that dissolves is the solute; water is the solvent.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting forms a new substance, iron oxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: 20 g of common salt is dissolved in 80 g of water. The mass percentage of the solution is
questions.explanation: Mass percentage = 20 / (20 + 80) × 100 = 20%.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The different dyes present in black ink can be separated by
questions.explanation: Different dyes travel at different rates on the paper in chromatography.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which method is best for getting pure crystals of copper sulphate from its impure solution?
questions.explanation: On cooling a hot saturated solution, pure crystals form and impurities stay in solution.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Nitrogen and oxygen of the air can be separated industrially by
options: fractional distillation of liquid air, using their different boiling points
evaporation of air at room temperature
questions.explanation: Air is cooled to a liquid and its gases boil off at different temperatures.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between a homogeneous and a heterogeneous mixture, giving one example of each.
questions.answer: A homogeneous mixture has uniform composition throughout, for example salt solution. A heterogeneous mixture has non-uniform composition with visible parts, for example sand and water.
questions.explanation: The difference lies in how uniformly the components are mixed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Is air a compound or a mixture? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: Air is a mixture. Its components (nitrogen, oxygen, etc.) are present in no fixed ratio that varies slightly from place to place, and each keeps its own properties. They can be separated by physical methods such as fractional distillation of liquid air.
questions.explanation: A compound would have fixed composition and properties unlike its elements.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many atoms are present in a molecule of oxygen, O2?
questions.explanation: The subscript 2 shows two atoms; oxygen is diatomic.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical formula of sodium chloride is
questions.explanation: Sodium has valency 1 and chlorine has valency 1, so they combine one to one.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: According to Dalton's atomic theory, atoms
options: can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction
can be divided into electrons and protons
can be seen with a simple microscope
questions.explanation: Dalton proposed that atoms are the basic indivisible particles and are only rearranged in reactions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical formula of aluminium oxide is
questions.explanation: Al has valency 3 and O has valency 2; criss-crossing gives Al2O3.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The mass of 1 mole of oxygen atoms is (atomic mass of O = 16 u)
questions.explanation: One mole of atoms has a mass equal to the atomic mass expressed in grams.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: One mole of carbon dioxide molecules contains how many moles of atoms?
questions.explanation: Each CO2 molecule has 1 carbon and 2 oxygen atoms, so there are 3 moles of atoms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In water, hydrogen and oxygen combine in the ratio 1 : 8 by mass. How much hydrogen is present in 18 g of water?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is 1/9 of the mass, so 18 × 1/9 = 2 g.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write the chemical formulae of calcium chloride and magnesium hydroxide.
questions.answer: Calcium has valency 2 and chloride has valency 1, so calcium chloride is CaCl2. Magnesium has valency 2 and hydroxide has valency 1, so magnesium hydroxide is Mg(OH)2.
questions.explanation: The formula balances the positive and negative charges.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Calculate the molar mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO3, and the mass of 0.2 mole of it. (Ca = 40 u, C = 12 u, O = 16 u)
questions.answer: Molar mass = 40 + 12 + 3 × 16 = 100 g/mol. Mass of 0.2 mole = 0.2 × 100 = 20 g.
questions.explanation: Mass of a sample is the number of moles times the molar mass.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Who proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus only in certain fixed shells?
questions.explanation: Bohr proposed that electrons stay in discrete orbits without radiating energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The mass of an electron compared with that of a proton is
questions.explanation: A proton is about 1836 times heavier than an electron.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A proton carries a
questions.explanation: Protons carry one unit of positive charge.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The mass number of an atom is the
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons make up almost all the mass; together they are called nucleons.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many neutrons are present in an atom of carbon-14 (atomic number 6)?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 14 − 6 = 8.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Isotopes of an element have the same
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ only in the number of neutrons, so their atomic number stays the same.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An atom has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 8. This atom is
options: chemically inert because its outermost shell is complete
questions.explanation: An octet in the outermost shell makes the atom stable, like argon.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write the electronic configuration and valency of magnesium (atomic number 12).
questions.answer: The electronic configuration is 2, 8, 2. Magnesium has two electrons in its outermost shell, which it can lose, so its valency is 2.
questions.explanation: Valency is the number of electrons lost, gained or shared to reach a full outer shell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties but different physical properties?
questions.answer: Chemical properties depend on the number and arrangement of electrons, which is the same for isotopes. Physical properties such as density and mass depend on the number of neutrons, which differs.
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ in mass number but not in atomic number.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Proteins are made in the cell by small structures called
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which part of the cell controls all its activities and contains the chromosomes?
questions.explanation: The nucleus directs the cell's activities and carries genetic material.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The green plastids that carry out photosynthesis are called
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following cells has no cell wall?
questions.explanation: Animal cells are bounded only by the plasma membrane.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Rough endoplasmic reticulum looks rough because
options: ribosomes are attached to its surface
it is covered with fat droplets
questions.explanation: Ribosomes on its surface give a rough appearance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The Golgi apparatus is mainly concerned with
options: storage, modification and packaging of substances
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages substances made in the ER for transport.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A plant cell placed in pure water swells but does not burst, unlike an animal cell, because the plant cell has
questions.explanation: The strong cell wall resists the pressure of the water that enters.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two functions of the plasma membrane.
questions.answer: The plasma membrane encloses the cell contents and separates the cell from its surroundings. It is selectively permeable, so it controls which substances enter and leave the cell.
keyPoints: Controls entry and exit of substances
questions.explanation: It acts as the cell's boundary and gatekeeper.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do muscle cells contain a large number of mitochondria?
questions.answer: Muscle cells are very active and need a lot of energy for contraction. Mitochondria release energy from food as ATP, so more mitochondria supply more energy.
keyPoints: Muscle cells need a lot of energy
questions.explanation: Number of mitochondria matches the energy needs of a cell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Fat is stored in the body in which tissue?
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue is a connective tissue that stores fat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which tissue forms the protective covering of the skin and the lining of the mouth?
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissues cover and line the body and its organs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Blood is a type of
questions.explanation: Blood is a fluid connective tissue that connects and transports.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a component of phloem?
questions.explanation: Sieve tubes carry food in phloem; tracheids and vessels belong to xylem.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In aquatic plants, parenchyma with large air cavities that helps them float is called
questions.explanation: Aerenchyma has air spaces that give buoyancy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which muscle cells are long, cylindrical, unbranched, striped and have many nuclei?
questions.explanation: These are the features of skeletal muscle fibres.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The tissue found at the joints that smoothens the bone surfaces and is also found in the nose, ear and trachea is
questions.explanation: Cartilage is a smooth, flexible connective tissue.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How does a ligament differ from a tendon?
questions.answer: A ligament connects one bone to another bone and is elastic, while a tendon connects muscle to bone and is strong with little elasticity.
questions.explanation: Both are connective tissues but they join different structures.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are the cells of the epithelium of the skin tightly packed with very little intercellular space?
questions.answer: The skin epithelium forms a barrier that protects the body from injury, germs and loss of water. Tightly packed cells leave no gaps through which these could pass.
keyPoints: No gaps for germs or water loss
questions.explanation: Structure suits function: protection needs a continuous layer.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Speed is calculated as
questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A body that covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, however small the intervals, is said to be in
questions.explanation: Equal distances in equal times is uniform motion.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The device in a vehicle that records the distance travelled is the
questions.explanation: The odometer shows the distance covered.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A straight sloping line in a velocity-time graph indicates
questions.explanation: A constant slope means the velocity changes by equal amounts in equal times.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The area under a velocity-time graph gives the
questions.explanation: Area under the velocity-time graph equals displacement.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A car starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 4 m/s². The distance covered in 3 s is
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½ × 4 × 9 = 18 m.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A stone tied to a string is whirled in a circle at a constant speed. Its velocity is changing because
options: its direction of motion keeps changing
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector, so a change in direction means a change in velocity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write the three equations of uniformly accelerated motion.
questions.answer: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as, where u is initial velocity, v is final velocity, a is acceleration, t is time and s is displacement.
questions.explanation: They hold when acceleration is constant.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A cyclist rides 6 km at 12 km/h and then another 6 km at 4 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
questions.answer: Time for the first part = 6/12 = 0.5 h; time for the second part = 6/4 = 1.5 h. Total distance = 12 km, total time = 2 h, so average speed = 12/2 = 6 km/h.
keyPoints: Time = distance / speed for each part
Average speed = total distance / total time = 6 km/h
questions.explanation: Average speed is not the simple average of the two speeds (8 km/h).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The inertia of a body depends on its
questions.explanation: Greater mass means greater inertia.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: According to Newton's third law, the action and reaction forces are
options: equal in magnitude and in the same direction
equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
questions.explanation: They are equal and opposite and act on two different bodies.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If the net force on an object that is at rest is zero, the object will
questions.explanation: Without an unbalanced force the state of rest does not change.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The momentum of a 3 kg object moving at 4 m/s is
questions.explanation: p = mv = 3 × 4 = 12 kg m/s.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following has the greatest inertia?
questions.explanation: The loaded truck has the greatest mass.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A 1000 kg car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 10 s. The net force on it is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A 5 kg trolley moving at 2 m/s hits an identical stationary 5 kg trolley and they move together. Their common velocity is
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 5 × 2 = (5 + 5) × v, so v = 1 m/s.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Define inertia and give one example of inertia of rest.
questions.answer: Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of rest or of uniform motion. Example: when a card under a coin on a glass is flicked away, the coin drops into the glass because it tends to stay at rest.
questions.explanation: The greater the mass of a body, the greater its inertia.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Using Newton's third law, explain how a swimmer moves forward.
questions.answer: The swimmer pushes the water backward with her hands and feet (action). The water pushes the swimmer forward with an equal and opposite force (reaction), so she moves forward.
questions.explanation: Action and reaction act on different bodies, so the swimmer can accelerate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The universal law of gravitation was given by
questions.explanation: Newton proposed the universal law of gravitation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of the universal gravitational constant G is
questions.explanation: From F = G m1 m2 / r², the unit of G is N m² kg⁻².

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An object is dropped from rest and falls freely for 2 s. Taking g = 9.8 m/s², its velocity after 2 s is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A body floats in a liquid when the density of the body is
options: much greater than that of the liquid
greater than that of the liquid
four times that of the liquid
less than that of the liquid
questions.explanation: If the body is less dense than the liquid, the upthrust exceeds its weight.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: It is easier to float in sea water than in river water because sea water
options: is denser and so exerts a larger upthrust for the same displaced volume
questions.explanation: Upthrust = density of liquid × volume displaced × g, so a denser liquid gives more upthrust.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person weighs 600 N on Earth. If the Moon's gravity is one-sixth of the Earth's, the person's weight on the Moon is
questions.explanation: Weight on the Moon = 600 / 6 = 100 N.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two differences between mass and weight.
questions.answer: Mass is the quantity of matter in a body; it is constant everywhere and is measured in kilograms. Weight is the force with which the Earth attracts the body; it changes from place to place and is measured in newtons.
keyPoints: Mass in kg, weight in N
questions.explanation: Weight = mass × g, so it depends on the local g.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a steel ship float while a steel needle sinks?
questions.answer: The hull of the ship is hollow and shaped to displace a large volume of water, so the upthrust equals its weight and its average density is less than that of water. A needle displaces little water, so the upthrust is less than its weight.
keyPoints: Ship displaces large volume of water
questions.explanation: Floating depends on the average density and the volume of liquid displaced.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In science, work done on an object is equal to
options: force times displacement in the direction of the force
questions.explanation: W = F × s when the displacement is along the force.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of power is the
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work; 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The energy stored in a stretched rubber band is
questions.explanation: A stretched band has stored (elastic potential) energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A man does 600 J of work in 20 s. His power is
questions.explanation: Power = work / time = 600 / 20 = 30 W.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a solar cell, the energy conversion is from
questions.explanation: Solar cells convert sunlight into electricity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upward. At its highest point
options: kinetic energy is maximum and potential energy is zero
kinetic energy is zero and potential energy is maximum
questions.explanation: The ball is momentarily at rest at the top, so all its energy there is potential.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Define 1 joule of work.
questions.answer: One joule is the work done when a force of 1 newton displaces an object by 1 metre in the direction of the force.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A force of 20 N moves a block 5 m along a smooth horizontal floor in the direction of the force. Find the work done and the kinetic energy gained if the block starts from rest.
questions.answer: Work done = 20 × 5 = 100 J. By the work-energy theorem all of this becomes kinetic energy, since the floor is smooth, so the gain in kinetic energy is 100 J.
keyPoints: Smooth floor so no energy lost to friction
questions.explanation: Work done on the block equals its gain in kinetic energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The repeated hearing of a sound after reflection from a distant surface is called
questions.explanation: A reflected sound heard separately is an echo.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Loudness of sound is measured in
questions.explanation: The decibel (dB) is the unit of sound level.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A sound wave of frequency 50 Hz travels at 340 m/s. Its wavelength is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sound of frequency above 20 000 Hz is called
questions.explanation: Sound above the human audible range is ultrasound.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A ship sends an ultrasonic pulse down and receives the echo from the sea floor after 4 s. If the speed of sound in sea water is 1500 m/s, the depth of the sea is
questions.explanation: The pulse travels down and up, so depth = 1500 × 4 / 2 = 3000 m.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Bats can detect obstacles in the dark by
options: emitting ultrasonic waves and detecting their echoes
questions.explanation: Bats use echolocation with ultrasound.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is reverberation? How can it be reduced in a big hall?
questions.answer: Reverberation is the persistence of sound in a hall due to repeated reflections from the walls and ceiling. It can be reduced by covering the walls and ceiling with sound-absorbing materials such as curtains, carpets and acoustic tiles.
keyPoints: Persistence of sound due to repeated reflection
Use of sound absorbers like curtains or carpets
questions.explanation: Excess reverberation makes speech unclear.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Astronauts on the Moon talk to each other using radio. Why can they not talk directly as on Earth?
questions.answer: The Moon has no atmosphere, so there is no air or other medium to carry sound waves. Radio waves are electromagnetic waves that can travel through a vacuum.
questions.explanation: Sound cannot pass through empty space.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a commonly used chemical fertiliser?
questions.explanation: Urea is a factory-made nitrogen fertiliser; the others are organic manures.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a pulse crop that is a good source of protein?
questions.explanation: Gram is a pulse; pulses give protein.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Hybridisation in crops means crossing between
options: plants of the same variety only
questions.explanation: Hybridisation crosses genetically dissimilar plants to combine useful traits.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Broilers are chickens raised mainly for
questions.explanation: Broilers are fed for fast growth to give meat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Poultry birds raised for egg production are called
questions.explanation: Layers are hens raised to lay eggs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is excessive use of chemical pesticides harmful?
options: It can pollute soil and water and enter the food chain
It helps bees to produce honey
questions.explanation: Pesticides can persist in the environment and accumulate in living things.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between kharif and rabi crops.
questions.answer: Kharif crops are grown in the rainy season from about June to October, for example paddy and maize. Rabi crops are grown in the winter season from about November to April, for example wheat and mustard.
questions.explanation: The two groups depend on the season and water needs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name two biotic and two abiotic factors that cause losses of stored grains.
questions.answer: Biotic factors are living causes such as insects, rodents, fungi and bacteria. Abiotic factors are non-living causes such as improper moisture and temperature in the place of storage.
keyPoints: Two biotic factors such as insects and rodents
Abiotic factors are moisture and temperature
questions.explanation: Good storage controls both groups of factors.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The change of a gas into a liquid is called
questions.explanation: On cooling, gas particles lose energy and come together to form a liquid, which is condensation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The change of a solid into a liquid at its melting point is called
questions.explanation: Melting is also called fusion.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a property of solids?
options: They take the shape of their container
They can be compressed a great deal
They have a fixed shape and negligible compressibility
questions.explanation: Solid particles are held in fixed positions, so a solid keeps its shape and is hard to compress.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Gases can be turned into liquids by
options: applying pressure and lowering the temperature
questions.explanation: Pressure and cooling push the particles close together so they form a liquid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Acetone evaporates faster than water at the same temperature because
options: the forces of attraction between its particles are weaker
questions.explanation: Weaker attractions let particles escape easily; acetone boils at a lower temperature than water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because
options: water boils at a lower temperature inside it
the increased pressure raises the boiling point, so the food is heated to a higher temperature
questions.explanation: Higher pressure raises the boiling point of water, so the contents become hotter than 100 °C.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ice at 0 °C cools a drink better than the same mass of water at 0 °C because the ice
options: absorbs extra heat (latent heat of fusion) in order to melt
questions.explanation: Melting ice takes in the latent heat of fusion from the drink.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a gas exert pressure on the walls of its container?
questions.answer: The particles of a gas move randomly at high speed and keep colliding with the walls of the container. The force of these collisions per unit area is the gas pressure.
keyPoints: Gas particles move randomly at high speed
Force per unit area is pressure
questions.explanation: More frequent or harder collisions mean higher pressure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe an activity to show that particles of matter are very small.
questions.answer: Dissolve two or three crystals of potassium permanganate in a glass of water and note the colour. Take a small amount of this solution and dilute it again and again with water. Even after many dilutions the water is still slightly coloured, which shows that a few crystals contain a huge number of tiny particles.
keyPoints: Dissolve a few crystals in water
questions.explanation: A visible colour after huge dilution means a tiny crystal contains a very large number of particles.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a suspension?
questions.explanation: In muddy water the solid particles are large and settle when left undisturbed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a compound?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is made of carbon and oxygen chemically combined.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An alloy is
options: a homogeneous mixture of metals, or of a metal and a non-metal
a suspension of a metal in water
questions.explanation: Alloys such as brass and steel are homogeneous mixtures.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A saturated solution is one in which
options: more solute can easily be added
no more solute can dissolve at that temperature
the solute is always a gas
questions.explanation: A saturated solution already holds the maximum amount of solute at that temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Cream is separated from milk by
questions.explanation: Spinning the milk quickly throws the denser parts outward and the lighter cream stays on top.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sugar cannot be separated from its aqueous solution by filtration because
options: the dissolved particles are smaller than the pores of the filter paper
questions.explanation: Dissolved particles are extremely small and pass through the filter paper.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When iron filings and sulphur are heated together, a black solid is formed which is not attracted by a magnet. This is a compound because it
options: is attracted by a magnet like iron
has a fixed composition and properties different from iron and sulphur
can be separated by a magnet
is still just a mixture of the two
questions.explanation: A new substance with different properties shows that a chemical combination has taken place.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the Tyndall effect? Why does it not occur in a true solution?
questions.answer: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of a beam of light by particles of a colloid or suspension, which makes the path of the beam visible. In a true solution the particles are too small to scatter light, so the beam is not visible.
questions.explanation: Only particles of larger size scatter light noticeably.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How can pure water be obtained from salt water? State the principle.
questions.answer: Salt water is heated in a distillation flask. The water evaporates, the vapour passes into a condenser where it cools back into liquid water, and the salt is left in the flask. The principle is that water and salt differ greatly in volatility.
keyPoints: Water vapour condensed in a condenser
questions.explanation: Only the volatile component, water, leaves the flask.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical symbol of iron is
questions.explanation: Fe comes from the Latin name ferrum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical symbol of potassium is
questions.explanation: K comes from the Latin name kalium.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The value of the Avogadro constant is
questions.explanation: One mole of any substance contains 6.022 × 10^23 particles.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The molecular mass of water (H = 1 u, O = 16 u) is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many moles are there in 36 g of water? (molar mass 18 g/mol)

questions.subject: science
questions.q: One mole of nitrogen gas, N2, contains how many moles of nitrogen atoms?
questions.explanation: Each N2 molecule has two atoms, so one mole of molecules has 2 moles of atoms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the mass of 3 moles of ammonia, NH3? (N = 14 u, H = 1 u)
questions.explanation: Molar mass = 14 + 3 = 17 g/mol, so 3 × 17 = 51 g.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a mole? How is it related to the Avogadro constant?
questions.answer: A mole is the amount of a substance that contains 6.022 × 10^23 particles (atoms, molecules or ions) of it. This number is the Avogadro constant, and one mole of a substance has a mass equal to its atomic or molecular mass in grams.
keyPoints: That number is the Avogadro constant
Mass of one mole is molar mass in grams
questions.explanation: The mole links the number of particles to measurable mass.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: 3 g of carbon combines with 8 g of oxygen to form carbon dioxide. How much oxygen is needed to burn 9 g of carbon completely to carbon dioxide? Which law do you use?
questions.answer: The ratio of carbon to oxygen by mass in carbon dioxide is fixed at 3 : 8. So 9 g of carbon needs 8 × 3 = 24 g of oxygen. This uses the law of constant proportions.
questions.explanation: A pure compound always has the same elements in the same mass ratio.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Atoms of the same element that have different mass numbers are called
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number but different numbers of neutrons.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which particle is present in the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The plum-pudding model of the atom was proposed by
questions.explanation: Thomson pictured electrons embedded in a positively charged sphere.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In Rutherford's experiment most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil. This showed that
options: most of the space inside an atom is empty
the atom is a solid sphere
electrons are heavier than alpha particles
questions.explanation: Particles went through undeflected because most of the atom is empty space.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many electrons does a sodium ion, Na+, have? (atomic number of sodium = 11)
questions.explanation: The atom has 11 electrons and Na+ has lost one, leaving 10.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The valency of oxygen (electronic configuration 2, 6) is
questions.explanation: Oxygen needs two more electrons to complete its octet, so its valency is 2.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 3. Its atomic number is
questions.explanation: The atom has 2 + 8 + 3 = 13 electrons, so its atomic number is 13.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between isotopes and isobars with one example of each.
questions.answer: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers, for example carbon-12 and carbon-14. Isobars are atoms of different elements with the same mass number but different atomic numbers, for example argon-40 and calcium-40.
keyPoints: Isotopes: same atomic number, different mass number
Isobars: same mass number, different atomic number
questions.explanation: The terms compare the atomic number and the mass number.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An atom X has 19 protons and 20 neutrons. Give its atomic number, mass number, electronic configuration and valency.
questions.answer: Atomic number = 19, mass number = 19 + 20 = 39. The electronic configuration is 2, 8, 8, 1. It has one electron in its outermost shell, so its valency is 1.
questions.explanation: The number of protons fixes the electrons of a neutral atom.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The smallest structural and functional unit of living organisms is the
questions.explanation: All living organisms are made of cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The jelly-like substance that fills the region between the nucleus and the plasma membrane is the
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm holds the cell organelles.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Plastids are found in
questions.explanation: Plastids such as chloroplasts occur in plant cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Oxygen enters a cell by moving from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration. This process is
questions.explanation: Movement of a substance from high to low concentration is diffusion; osmosis refers only to water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An amoeba takes in food by engulfing it with its flexible plasma membrane. This process is called
questions.explanation: Endocytosis is the taking in of materials by the cell membrane folding around them.

Only plants are made of cells
All living things are made of cells and new cells arise from pre-existing cells
Cells are not found in animals

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two differences between a plant cell and an animal cell.
questions.answer: A plant cell has a cell wall outside the plasma membrane, but an animal cell does not. A plant cell has plastids and a large central vacuole, while an animal cell has no plastids and only small vacuoles.
keyPoints: Cell wall only in plant cells
questions.explanation: These differences are linked to the plant's way of making its own food and keeping its shape.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What would happen if the plasma membrane of a cell were ruptured?
questions.answer: The cell contents would leak out and the cell could no longer control which substances enter or leave. The internal environment of the cell would be lost and the cell would die.
keyPoints: Control over entry and exit is lost
questions.explanation: The membrane keeps the cell contents separate from the outside.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Suberin makes the cork waterproof, so it protects the plant.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the four types of animal tissue and give one function of each.
questions.answer: Epithelial tissue covers and protects the body surfaces. Connective tissue joins and supports organs, for example bone or blood. Muscular tissue helps movement. Nervous tissue carries messages as impulses.
questions.explanation: Each tissue is specialised for a different job.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How is the structure of a neuron suited to its function?
questions.answer: A neuron has a cell body with a nucleus and long thin extensions. Short branched dendrites receive impulses and a long axon carries the impulse over long distances to other cells, so a neuron can carry messages quickly throughout the body.
questions.explanation: Long extensions let one cell reach far-off parts of the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is uniform circular motion? Give an example.
questions.answer: Uniform circular motion is motion of a body along a circular path with constant speed. Its velocity changes continuously because its direction keeps changing. An example is the motion of a stone tied to a string whirled in a circle, or the tip of a clock's hand.
keyPoints: Direction, and so velocity, keeps changing
questions.explanation: Although speed is constant the motion is accelerated.

questions.answer: When two or more objects interact, the total momentum of the objects before the interaction equals the total momentum after it, provided no external unbalanced force acts on them.
questions.explanation: It follows from Newton's second and third laws.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a boat move backward when a person jumps forward from it onto the shore?
questions.answer: When the person pushes the boat backward to jump forward, the boat pushes the person forward with an equal and opposite force (third law). The boat gets momentum in the opposite direction, so it moves backward.
keyPoints: Equal and opposite reaction on person
Boat moves backward by conservation of momentum
questions.explanation: Total momentum remains zero, so the two move in opposite directions.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: The pull of the Earth on objects is the gravitational force.

questions.explanation: Free fall is motion under gravity with no other force.

has a larger area, so there is more pressure
questions.explanation: Pressure is inversely proportional to the area on which the force acts.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A wooden block of density 600 kg/m³ is placed in water of density 1000 kg/m³. The block will
options: float with part of it above the water
float completely submerged at any depth
questions.explanation: Its density is less than that of water, so it floats with part above the surface.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is buoyancy (upthrust)? On what does it depend?
questions.answer: Buoyancy is the upward force exerted by a liquid or gas on an object immersed in it. It depends on the density of the fluid and on the volume of the fluid displaced by the object.
questions.explanation: By Archimedes' principle the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do tractors and heavy vehicles have wide tyres?
questions.answer: A wide tyre spreads the weight of the vehicle over a large area. Since pressure is force divided by area, the pressure on the ground is smaller, so the vehicle does not sink into soft soil.
keyPoints: Vehicle does not sink in soft ground
questions.explanation: The same weight gives less pressure if the area is greater.

questions.subject: science

options: A boy stands holding a bag
A man pushes a wall that does not move
A boy pushes a cart and it moves
questions.explanation: Work needs a force that produces a displacement.

options: its potential energy has decreased and its kinetic energy has increased
questions.explanation: Potential energy changes into kinetic energy as the stone falls.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between kinetic energy and potential energy with one example of each.
questions.answer: Kinetic energy is the energy a body has because of its motion, for example a moving car. Potential energy is the energy a body has because of its position or state, for example a stone held at a height or a stretched spring.
keyPoints: PE is due to position or state
questions.explanation: Both are forms of mechanical energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A boy of mass 50 kg climbs 30 steps, each 20 cm high, in 1 minute. Find the work done and his power. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer: Total height = 30 × 0.2 = 6 m. Work done = mgh = 50 × 10 × 6 = 3000 J. Power = work / time = 3000 / 60 = 50 W.
questions.explanation: The work done against gravity is mgh and power is work per unit time.

questions.explanation: Sound is faster in solids than in liquids and gases, and cannot travel in vacuum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What does SONAR stand for? State one use.
questions.answer: SONAR stands for Sound Navigation And Ranging. It uses ultrasonic waves to find the depth of the sea or to locate objects such as submarines and shoals of fish under water.
keyPoints: Finds depth or locates objects under water
questions.explanation: The time taken by the echo gives the distance.

questions.answer: Speed v = f × λ = 2000 × 0.4 = 800 m/s. Time = distance / speed = 1500 / 800 = 1.875 s.
questions.explanation: Convert kHz to Hz and cm to m before using v = fλ.

questions.explanation: Wheat, rice and maize are cereals rich in carbohydrates.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is vermicompost good for the soil?
options: It reduces the water-holding capacity of soil
It improves the fertility and structure of the soil
questions.explanation: Vermicompost is organic, adds nutrients and humus and improves soil structure.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name two sources of water used for irrigation in India.
questions.answer: Common sources of irrigation include wells, canals, river lift systems and tanks.
questions.explanation: The choice depends on the region and the availability of water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why should a farmer not depend on chemical fertilisers alone year after year?
questions.answer: Continued use of chemical fertilisers alone reduces the organic matter and microorganisms in the soil and damages its structure and fertility. They can also pollute water through run-off. Adding manure or compost along with fertilisers keeps the soil healthy.
keyPoints: Reduces soil organic matter and organisms
questions.explanation: Balanced use of organic and inorganic inputs is better for the soil.

questions.explanation: Matter has mass and occupies space; light is a form of energy and has neither.

questions.explanation: Air that already holds a lot of water vapour takes up less vapour from the liquid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A desert cooler works better on a dry day than on a humid day because

evaporation of water is faster when the air has low humidity
the water in the cooler is colder on dry days
the fan runs faster on dry days
questions.explanation: Faster evaporation of water removes more heat and gives more cooling.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When ice at 0 °C changes to water at 0 °C, which statement is correct?
options: The particles gain energy and move more freely
There is no change in the energy of the particles
questions.explanation: Heat absorbed during melting increases the energy of the particles, so they can move more freely.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: The kelvin scale starts at 273 below the Celsius zero (rounded).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does water in an earthen pot (matka) become cool in summer?
questions.answer: The earthen pot has very tiny pores through which water seeps to the outer surface and evaporates. The evaporation takes heat from the water in the pot, so the water becomes cool.
keyPoints: Evaporation takes heat from the water inside
questions.explanation: Evaporation causes cooling.

questions.explanation: Elements are grouped by properties into metals, non-metals and metalloids.

questions.answer: In a true solution the particles are very small, do not settle and pass through filter paper, and the solution is transparent. In a suspension the particles are large, settle on standing, can be filtered out and the mixture is opaque or cloudy.
keyPoints: Particles of true solution are tiny
Suspension can be filtered, solution cannot
questions.explanation: The difference lies mainly in particle size.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How will you separate (a) a mixture of kerosene oil and water and (b) a mixture of ethanol and water?
questions.answer: (a) Kerosene and water are immiscible, so they are separated by a separating funnel, where the lower layer is run off. (b) Ethanol and water are miscible but have different boiling points, so they are separated by fractional distillation, in which the ethanol, which boils first, is collected.
keyPoints: Miscible liquids with different boiling points use distillation
questions.explanation: The method is chosen from the property that differs between the liquids.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State any two postulates of Dalton's atomic theory.
questions.answer: All matter is made of very small particles called atoms, which cannot be divided or created or destroyed in a chemical reaction. Atoms of the same element are identical in mass and properties, while atoms of different elements have different masses and properties.
questions.explanation: Later discoveries showed that atoms can be divided into subatomic particles and that isotopes exist.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Find the number of atoms in 0.1 mole of water, H2O. (Avogadro constant = 6.022 × 10^23)
questions.answer: Number of molecules = 0.1 × 6.022 × 10^23 = 6.022 × 10^22. Each molecule has 3 atoms, so the number of atoms = 3 × 6.022 × 10^22 = 1.8066 × 10^23.
questions.explanation: Multiply the number of molecules by the atoms per molecule.

questions.explanation: The outermost shell of sodium has one electron.

questions.subject: science

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The valency of neon (electronic configuration 2, 8) is
questions.explanation: Its outer shell is complete, so it neither gains nor loses electrons.

questions.explanation: The atom has 17 electrons, and the ion has gained one, giving 18.

questions.explanation: F has 9 electrons and F− has gained one, giving 10.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two postulates of Bohr's model of the atom.
questions.answer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus only in certain special orbits (shells) called discrete orbits. While an electron stays in one of these orbits it does not radiate energy.
keyPoints: No energy is radiated in these orbits
questions.explanation: This explained why the atom is stable.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain how sodium and chlorine atoms each acquire a stable electronic arrangement when they form sodium chloride.
questions.answer: A sodium atom (2, 8, 1) loses one electron to become Na+ (2, 8), and a chlorine atom (2, 8, 7) gains that electron to become Cl− (2, 8, 8). Both then have complete outer shells, and the oppositely charged ions attract each other to form NaCl.
keyPoints: Both get a complete outer shell
questions.explanation: Atoms combine to reach the stable octet.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Leeuwenhoek first saw living cells using his own microscope.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Chromosomes in the nucleus are made of DNA and proteins.

questions.explanation: Bacteria have no membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.q: The plasma membrane is said to be selectively permeable because it

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A dry raisin swells when placed in water. This is because
options: water enters the raisin by osmosis since the water concentration is lower inside it
questions.explanation: Water moves from a higher to a lower water concentration through the raisin's membrane.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are chromosomes? State their role.
questions.answer: Chromosomes are thread-like structures in the nucleus, made of DNA and proteins, which become visible when the cell divides. They carry the genes and pass on characters from parents to offspring.
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are the carriers of heredity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Under a microscope a student sees a cell with a cell wall, a large central vacuole and chloroplasts. Identify the type of cell and give two reasons.
questions.answer: It is a plant cell. Cell walls and chloroplasts occur only in plant cells and not in animal cells, and a large central vacuole is also a typical feature of plant cells.
questions.explanation: These features separate plant cells from animal cells.

questions.explanation: Calcium and phosphorus compounds make bone hard.

questions.subject: science
