options: Its cells are spindle-shaped with a single nucleus
Its cells are striped with many nuclei
It is found in the limbs
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle cells are spindle-shaped, unstriped and involuntary, as in the intestine.

questions.answer: Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing cells. Its cells are thin-walled, closely packed with dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus, and they have little or no vacuole.
questions.explanation: These features suit the job of making new cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How do plants increase in length and in thickness? Name the tissues responsible.
questions.answer: Plants grow in length because of the apical meristem at the tips of roots and shoots. They grow in thickness because of the lateral meristem (cambium) present along the sides of stems and roots.
keyPoints: Thickness by lateral meristem or cambium
questions.explanation: Each growth direction depends on a different meristem.

questions.explanation: Speed does not tell the direction; velocity does.

questions.explanation: Change in momentum = 0.01 × 400 = 4 kg m/s, so F = 4 / 0.01 = 400 N.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between balanced and unbalanced forces.
questions.answer: Balanced forces are forces that cancel each other so that the net force is zero and the state of motion does not change. Unbalanced forces have a non-zero net force, which changes the speed or direction of motion of the body.
keyPoints: Balanced: net force zero, no change in motion
Unbalanced: net force non-zero, motion changes
questions.explanation: Only an unbalanced force produces acceleration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a loaded truck need a larger force to stop in the same time than an empty truck moving at the same speed?
questions.answer: The loaded truck has a greater mass, so at the same speed it has a greater momentum. To change this momentum to zero in the same time needs a greater force, since force equals the rate of change of momentum.
questions.explanation: Greater momentum means a greater force for the same stopping time.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of density is
questions.explanation: Density is mass per unit volume.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: This is Archimedes' principle.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Buoyant force = loss of apparent weight = 50 − 30 = 20 N.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: We feel lighter when we are in water because

questions.explanation: The upthrust of water partly balances our weight.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: At a distance from the Earth's centre equal to twice the Earth's radius, the acceleration due to gravity is (g = value at the surface)
questions.explanation: g varies inversely as the square of the distance, so doubling the distance divides g by four.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is free fall? What is the acceleration of a freely falling body near the Earth?
questions.answer: Free fall is the motion of a body falling towards the Earth under the force of gravity alone, with no air resistance. Its acceleration is about 9.8 m/s² for all bodies.
questions.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity does not depend on the mass of the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A stone of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 20 m. Find its velocity just before it hits the ground. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer: Using v² = u² + 2gh with u = 0: v² = 2 × 10 × 20 = 400, so v = 20 m/s.
questions.explanation: The mass of the stone does not affect its speed in free fall.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Work done by a force is positive when the force and the displacement are
questions.explanation: A force along the displacement does positive work.

questions.explanation: Electricity bills are in units of kilowatt-hours.

questions.explanation: KE equals the loss of potential energy: mgh = 2 × 10 × 10 = 200 J.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is power? State its SI unit.
questions.answer: Power is the rate of doing work, or the work done per unit time (P = W / t). Its SI unit is the watt (W), and 1 W = 1 J/s.
questions.explanation: A machine that does the same work faster has more power.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A pump raises 100 kg of water to a height of 10 m in 20 s. Find the power of the pump. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer: Work done = mgh = 100 × 10 × 10 = 10 000 J. Power = work / time = 10 000 / 20 = 500 W.
questions.explanation: Work against gravity divided by time gives the power.

questions.q: The relation between frequency f and time period T of a wave is
questions.explanation: Frequency is the reciprocal of the time period.

questions.explanation: Sound travels at roughly 340 m/s in air.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: A higher frequency gives a higher pitch, which is heard as a shriller sound.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two uses of ultrasound.
questions.answer: Ultrasound is used to clean delicate parts such as electronic components, to detect flaws and cracks in metal blocks, and in ultrasonography to image organs inside the body.
questions.explanation: Ultrasound can reach places that are hard to reach and can reveal hidden structures.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person standing 25 m from a high wall claps his hands. Will he hear a distinct echo? Take the speed of sound as 344 m/s and the minimum time gap for a distinct echo as 0.1 s.
questions.answer: The sound travels 25 m to the wall and 25 m back, a total of 50 m. Time = 50 / 344 = about 0.145 s. This is more than 0.1 s, so he will hear a distinct echo.
keyPoints: Greater than 0.1 s so echo is heard
questions.explanation: An echo is heard separately if it arrives at least 0.1 s after the original sound.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Separating the grain from the chaff using wind is called
questions.explanation: In winnowing, the lighter chaff is blown away by the wind.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Milch animals are cows and buffaloes kept for milk.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Marine fisheries are in sea water, while inland fisheries are in fresh water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Legumes improve soil fertility because bacteria in their root nodules
questions.explanation: Root nodule bacteria convert nitrogen of the air into usable compounds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Plants require 16 nutrients. How many of these are supplied by the soil?
questions.explanation: Air and water supply three of the nutrients; the soil supplies the other 13.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An advantage of manure that chemical fertilisers do not have is that manure
options: has a high percentage of nutrients
adds humus and improves the structure of the soil
questions.explanation: Manure is rich in organic matter that improves soil structure and water retention.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the two kinds of fisheries and give a difference between them.
questions.answer: The two kinds are marine fisheries and inland fisheries. Marine fisheries are in the sea and use sea water, while inland fisheries are in fresh water such as rivers, canals and ponds.
questions.explanation: Fish are obtained from both sea and fresh water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is bee-keeping useful to farmers apart from giving honey?
questions.answer: Bees visit flowers to collect nectar and pollen and in doing so they carry pollen from flower to flower, which helps pollination and increases crop yield. Beeswax is also obtained.
questions.explanation: Bee-keeping on a farm supports the production of crops that depend on pollination.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In which state of matter do particles only vibrate about fixed positions?
questions.explanation: Particles of a solid are held in fixed positions and can only vibrate.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Gas particles move freely with large spaces between them, so they mix fastest.

questions.explanation: This is the latent heat of fusion.

questions.explanation: Naphthalene changes directly from solid to vapour.

questions.explanation: Applying pressure turns a large volume of gas into a small volume of liquid.

questions.subject: science

options: move freely in all directions and have negligible attraction between them
questions.explanation: With very weak attractions the particles spread to occupy all the space available.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Water keeps boiling at 100 °C even though heat is supplied continuously, because
options: the heat supplied is used to change the liquid into vapour (latent heat)
the water loses all its heat to the pan
questions.explanation: The heat goes into overcoming particle attractions rather than raising the temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two characteristics of the particles of matter.
questions.answer: The particles of matter are very small and have spaces between them. They are continuously moving, and they attract each other.
questions.explanation: These ideas explain diffusion and the three states of matter.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do water droplets form on the outer surface of a glass containing ice-cold water?
questions.answer: Water vapour present in the air comes in contact with the cold surface of the glass and loses energy. It condenses into tiny droplets of liquid water on the outside of the glass.
questions.explanation: The water does not pass through the glass; it comes from the air.

questions.explanation: Iron is attracted by a magnet but sulphur is not.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: To purify copper sulphate, crystallisation is preferred over simple evaporation to dryness because
options: crystallisation gives pure crystals and leaves impurities in the solution, while evaporation may leave impurities behind or decompose the solid
questions.explanation: On cooling a saturated solution pure crystals separate, while the impurities remain dissolved.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is chromatography? Give one use.
questions.answer: Chromatography is a method for separating the components of a mixture that dissolve in the same solvent, based on their different rates of movement over a paper or other material. It is used to separate dyes in ink or colours in a dye.
questions.explanation: Components that dissolve better in the solvent travel farther.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Classify each of the following as an element, a compound or a mixture: sea water, hydrogen, sodium chloride, steel.
questions.answer: Sea water is a mixture. Hydrogen is an element. Sodium chloride is a compound. Steel is a mixture (an alloy of iron and carbon).
questions.explanation: Elements and compounds are pure substances; mixtures have two or more substances physically combined.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: The atom is the smallest particle of an element taking part in reactions.

questions.explanation: The standard for atomic mass is the carbon-12 atom.

questions.explanation: The subscript 3 shows three oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: science

questions.answer: Calcium is Ca, copper is Cu, chlorine is Cl and nitrogen is N.
questions.explanation: Symbols may be one or two letters, with the first capital and the second small.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: On heating 10 g of calcium carbonate, 5.6 g of calcium oxide and 4.4 g of carbon dioxide are obtained. Which law does this verify? Explain.
questions.answer: It verifies the law of conservation of mass. The mass of the products is 5.6 + 4.4 = 10 g, which equals the mass of the reactant, so no mass is lost or gained.
questions.explanation: The total mass is the same before and after the reaction.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons are packed together in the nucleus.

questions.explanation: The number of protons equals the number of electrons, so the charges cancel.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Electrons occupy shells around the nucleus.

questions.explanation: It has two electrons in the outermost shell, which it can lose.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number (17) but different mass numbers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two uses of isotopes.
questions.answer: An isotope of uranium is used as a fuel in nuclear reactors. An isotope of cobalt is used in the treatment of cancer, and an isotope of iodine is used in the treatment of goitre.
questions.explanation: Any two valid uses are acceptable.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does the atomic number, and not the mass number, identify an element?
questions.answer: The atomic number is the number of protons, which is fixed for each element. Atoms of the same element can have different mass numbers (isotopes), and atoms of different elements can have the same mass number (isobars), so mass number cannot identify an element.
keyPoints: Atomic number is the number of protons
questions.explanation: Only the proton number is the same for all atoms of one element.

questions.explanation: Amoeba consists of a single cell.

questions.explanation: The nuclear membrane has pores for the exchange of materials.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Vacuoles in plant cells are filled with
options: cell sap containing water, sugars and wastes
questions.explanation: The large vacuole stores water, sugars, amino acids and waste substances.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which organelle is found in both plant and animal cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria occur in both kinds of cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The endoplasmic reticulum serves as
options: a channel for transport of materials within the cell
a store of the cell's DNA
questions.explanation: ER is a network of membranes that carries materials through the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The plasma membrane is made mainly of
questions.explanation: It is organised as a layer of lipids with proteins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Onion peel cells are placed in a strong salt solution. The cell contents shrink away from the cell wall because
options: the cell absorbs water and bursts
water leaves the cell by osmosis
salt enters and makes the cell divide
questions.explanation: Water moves out into the more concentrated solution, and the protoplasm shrinks (plasmolysis).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is diffusion? Give an example of its importance in cells.
questions.answer: Diffusion is the spontaneous movement of a substance from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration. For example, oxygen diffuses into the cell and carbon dioxide diffuses out of the cell.
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the main way in which gases are exchanged by cells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is the cell called the structural and functional unit of life?
questions.answer: All living organisms are made of cells, so the cell is the structural unit. Each cell can carry out the basic functions of life such as taking in food, respiration and removing wastes, so it is also the functional unit.
keyPoints: Cell is the smallest living unit
questions.explanation: Even single cells such as amoeba perform all life processes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a permanent tissue?
questions.explanation: Parenchyma is a simple permanent tissue; the others are meristems.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Intercalary meristem is found
options: at the base of leaves or internodes
questions.explanation: It adds length at the base of leaves and internodes, as in grasses.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Phloem transports
questions.explanation: Phloem carries sugars made by photosynthesis to all parts of the plant.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ciliated epithelium in the windpipe helps to
options: move mucus and dust out of the respiratory tract
questions.explanation: The cilia beat to push mucus and trapped particles out.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which muscle is found only in the heart?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle forms the wall of the heart.

questions.explanation: Wood is mostly xylem that has built up over the years.

questions.subject: science

questions.explanation: Columnar epithelium helps movement of substances across the lining.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two functions of areolar tissue.
questions.answer: Areolar tissue fills the space inside organs and supports internal organs. It also helps in the repair of tissues.
questions.explanation: It is a connective tissue found between the skin and muscles and around organs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How is the structure of sclerenchyma suited to its function?
questions.answer: Sclerenchyma cells are dead and have thick walls hardened with lignin, and there is almost no space between the cells. This makes the tissue strong and rigid, so it gives mechanical support to the plant.
keyPoints: Dead cells with thick lignified walls
questions.explanation: Structure and function are matched in each tissue.

questions.explanation: Speed has magnitude only; the others have direction too.

questions.answer: The slope of a distance-time graph represents the speed of the body. For a body at rest the distance does not change with time, so the graph is a straight line parallel to the time axis.
questions.explanation: A steeper line means a faster body.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s. Find the maximum height it reaches and the time taken to reach it. (g = 10 m/s²)

questions.explanation: Friction opposes the motion and slows the ball.

options: A book stays at rest on a table
A coin falls into a glass when the card under it is flicked
Dust falls out when a carpet is beaten
A passenger leans forward when a moving bus brakes suddenly
questions.explanation: The passenger's body tends to continue moving forward.

half that of the 4 kg body
twice that of the 4 kg body
four times that of the 4 kg body

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Give two examples of Newton's third law in everyday life.
questions.answer: When we walk, we push the ground backward and the ground pushes us forward. When a balloon releases air backward, the air pushes the balloon forward. A rocket and the recoil of a gun are also examples.
questions.explanation: Any two correct examples with the action and reaction identified are acceptable.

the objects are always far apart
the force between them is repulsive

questions.explanation: g decreases slightly with height, so the weight decreases a little.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between the universal gravitational constant G and the acceleration due to gravity g.
questions.answer: G is a constant with the same value everywhere in the universe (6.67 × 10^-11 N m²/kg²). The value of g is about 9.8 m/s² on the surface of the Earth and changes from place to place, for example with height and on other planets.
keyPoints: g varies from place to place
questions.explanation: g depends on G, the mass and the radius of the planet.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An object weighs 10 N on the Earth. Find its mass and its weight on the Moon, where gravity is one-sixth of the Earth's. (g = 10 m/s² on Earth)
questions.answer: Mass = weight / g = 10 / 10 = 1 kg, which is the same on the Moon. Weight on the Moon = 10 / 6 = about 1.67 N.
questions.explanation: Only the weight, not the mass, changes with gravity.
